To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression and processing of the APP gene is regulated by epigenetic factors, such as DNA methylation, chromatin structure and RNA-binding proteins.

1) APP gene is epigenetically regulated in the control of its expression, and 2) APP pre-mRNA undergoes alternative splicing in a tissue-dependent manner, and 3) the APP gene undergoes genomic rearrangements in a tissue-dependent and age-dependent manner.

(1) the APP gene undergoes alternative pre-mRNA splicings and genomic rearrangements, which may affect the expression levels of APP isoforms and the generation of Aβ peptides in the brains of LNS patients; (2) the APP gene may be a candidate gene for FXS and AD, and (3) the APP gene is a potential target for antisense drugs in the treatment of AD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of APP, and its epigenetic aspects in particular, and how these findings may be related to the neuropathology of LNS, FXS and AD.
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the role of APP, its isoforms and its epigenetic control in normal development and disease.
the role of the APP gene in the etiology of LNS and LNVs, and in the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of FXS, autism and AD.
